races.name: BOYLE Sports Money Back If 2nd To SP Fav Handicap

runners_data.name: Baggot Street
runners_data.note: Front-runner with blinkers whose recent C&D win gives confidence but faces stronger pace pressure here
runners_data.comment: Ex Charlie Johnston; wears blinkers for the first time on yard debut
runners_data.spotlight: Ran well in defeat on multiple occasions for Charlie Johnston at 6f/7f; sported first-time blinkers when running out a surprise 33-1 winner on stable/seasonal debut at Navan (6f, yielding) 13 days ago; should go well again.

runners_data.name: This Guy
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who showed best form in winter at Dundalk but drops in class after modest Curragh effort
runners_data.comment: Maiden looked on the verge of AW success during the winter, unplaced at Naas last Monday
runners_data.spotlight: Maiden was runner-up three times in a row at Dundalk during the winter; not as good in recent months; midfield in 6f Curragh handicap on latest but this is an ease in grade; Colin Keane takes over; high draw not ideal.

runners_data.name: Love Bomb
runners_data.note: Prominent type who won C&D off higher mark but tends to fade in finish and has been disappointing this season
runners_data.comment: Won off 6lb lower last year, yet to fire this term, 3lb wrong, others preferred
runners_data.spotlight: Won C&D handicap (yielding) last September off 3lb higher; yet to really fire this term but takes a big drop in class after a poor run at the Curragh 10 days ago; drawn widest of all.

runners_data.name: Plushy
runners_data.note: Front-runner with 0-10 record but has placed twice in similar company and should appreciate return to 5f
runners_data.comment: Some good runs in defeat on turf and AW, weighted to reverse Jan' form with Stone Bear
runners_data.spotlight: Record is 0-10 but has run well in defeat; placed on first two starts in 5f maidens last year at Bellewstown (good) and Cork (good to firm); excuses for Naas flop on latest as fly leapt the stalls; contender eased in grade.

runners_data.name: Cashel Blue
runners_data.note: Prominent runner making handicap debut who may improve significantly from previous maiden form on softer ground
runners_data.comment: Well beaten both starts at Cork over 5f and 6f, qualifies for handicaps after this
runners_data.spotlight: Failed to fire in three maidens at 5f/6f on yielding/soft ground, the latest of those at Navan 13 days ago when beaten 11.5l into fifth; likely improver now handicapping; worth a market check.

runners_data.name: Spirit Above
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse making turf debut after 58-day break with little sign of winning potential in previous starts
runners_data.comment: No sign yet of winning potential, can only be watched in first turf handicap
runners_data.spotlight: Showed no signs of winning potential in maidens or on handicap debut at Dundalk (6f) on latest; can only be watched down in trip in first turf handicap.

runners_data.name: Spiced Gold
runners_data.note: Front-runner with fading tendency who was tailed off behind Baggot Street 13 days ago and looks outclassed
runners_data.comment: Unexposed 3yo making handicap debut after 3 undistinguished runs as a 2yo; best watched
runners_data.spotlight: Three undistinguished runs as a 2yo; tailed off behind Baggot Street on handicap/seasonal debut at Navan 13 days ago; best watched.

runners_data.name: Hooves Your Daddy
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with fading concerns but showed promise when runner-up at Dundalk after 36-day break
runners_data.comment: Best effort came in Naas maiden but way out of form last twice in h'caps; off 206 days
runners_data.spotlight: Fair effort when fifth in Naas maiden in August (6f, good); struggled in following three runs but back from a break when runner-up at Dundalk last month (5f; had Love Bomb, Plushy and Lady Landhort behind); entitled to respect back on turf.

runners_data.name: Mini Cotai
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who shaped well when third at Dundalk in January and gets significant weight relief here
runners_data.comment: Not a bad run at Dundalk on penultimate, off since January, probably best watched
runners_data.spotlight: Modest form in good-ground turf maidens last year; shaped well over 6f at Dundalk in January when third; back from short break when giving way late on to finish fourth, beaten 1.5l in first turf handicap at Cork (5f, soft); 2lb wrong.

runners_data.name: Lady Landhort
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with fading tendency whose sole win came at Dundalk off much lower mark in March
runners_data.comment: AW win off 3lb lower in March, beaten off revised mark since, others appeal more
runners_data.spotlight: Sole success came in 6f Dundalk handicap in March off 49; came up short off revised mark twice since, one place behind Hooves Your Daddy over 5f at Dundalk on latest; 3lb lower on first turf handicap; in the mix.

races.paceDynamic: Baggot Street, Plushy, and Spiced Gold will ensure a genuine gallop from the off over this minimum trip. The confirmed front-runners will set a strong pace that should stretch the field, with This Guy and Love Bomb likely pressing from prominent positions. The combination of good ground and sustained speed will test stamina reserves in the final furlong, creating opportunities for those who can quicken off the pace. This race shape strongly favours prominent runners and hold-up horses with tactical speed over pure front-runners who may pay for early exertions.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Strong Pace Suits Closers
scenarios.trigger: If the three front-runners go hard early and create a strong gallop
scenarios.body: The pace will stretch the field and set up perfectly for horses with finishing kicks to pick off tiring leaders. Hold-up horses like Mini Cotai and Hooves Your Daddy can capitalize on their tactical speed.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tactics Prevail
scenarios.trigger: If This Guy and Love Bomb can sit handy without getting involved in pace battle
scenarios.body: They can track the early speed and have enough left to outstay the front-runners while holding off late closers. The prominent position offers the perfect compromise.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Baggot Street can dictate a more moderate pace despite the other pace angles
scenarios.body: The recent winner can use proven stamina to kick clear when others come under pressure. Blinkers and confidence from last win could prove decisive.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the front-runners go too fast and all three tie up dramatically
scenarios.body: The race becomes a sprint finish between whoever has anything left, likely favoring those who stayed out of early trouble. Form and class become secondary to positioning.

watchPoints.text: Spiced Gold and Plushy could set unsustainable fractions if they battle for early lead alongside Baggot Street
Love Bomb's tendency to fade in the finish makes her vulnerable if the pace is genuine over this minimum trip
Mini Cotai gets a 27lb weight swing with Baggot Street from their Navan meeting and could be overpriced
Several runners including Spirit Above and Lady Landhort return from lengthy breaks without recent turf form
Three apprentice riders take 7lb claims which could prove decisive in a competitive handicap

races.name: BOYLE Sports Money Back Meetings Every Day Fillies & Mares Maiden

runners_data.name: Youse Raven Mad
runners_data.note: Debut runner with no form guide but carries decent breeding credentials as a Raven's Pass filly
runners_data.spotlight: Raven's Pass filly; 16,000euros yearling; half-sister to winners High Fibre and Granary Queen; dam 7.4f 2yo/1m winner (72), half-sister to Australian 1m4f Group 3 winner Caravan Rolls On; best watched.

runners_data.name: Courtlough Gula
runners_data.note: Showed nothing when tailed off at 200-1 on debut and returns after 253 days off the track
runners_data.spotlight: Sent off 200-1 for 7f Naas debut last September and failed to beat a single rival home.

runners_data.name: Dandymaria
runners_data.note: Sister to Listed-placed winner making debut for trainer Oliver who has solid recent strike-rate
runners_data.spotlight: Dandy Man filly; 23,000euros yearling; sister to Listed-placed 5f-6.5f winner Whistle And Flute (inc 2yo; RPR 106); dam unraced half-sister to 1m 2yo Group 2 winner Agnes Stewart and 1m5f Listed winner Sorrel; watch betting.

runners_data.name: Ruby Vega
runners_data.note: Debutant with 10lb claiming rider but brings half-sister to winner pedigree
runners_data.spotlight: Lucky Vega filly; 19,000euros foal; half-sister to 5f winner; dam unplaced, half-sister to 5f Group 3 winner Came From The Dark, out of Group-placed 7f winning half-sister to 6f Group 1 winner Pipalong; watch.

runners_data.name: Sioux The Boss
runners_data.note: Expensive yearling making debut with strong staying pedigree through dam's family
runners_data.comment: Sioux Nation filly cost 70,000euros as a yearling; worth a market check on debut
runners_data.spotlight: Sioux Nation filly; 70,000euros yearling; half-sister to four winners inc Measure Of Time (French 1m1f-1m6f inc 2yo/Listed; RPR 102); dam unraced sister to 1m2f/1m4f Listed Flat winner and smart jumper Stage Affair.

runners_data.name: Rebel Wave
runners_data.note: Showed promise when fifth on debut 12 days ago and can improve markedly for the experience
runners_data.comment: E280,000 New Bay filly, dam 7f US dirt winner, could go well, market best guide
runners_data.spotlight: New Bay filly's price rose from 110,000gns as a yearling to 280,000euros as a foal; looked in need of the run when fifth of eight on Naas debut (1m, good) 12 days ago; should strip fitter now.

runners_data.name: What About Us
runners_data.note: Hit the frame twice before good second to subsequent Group 1 entry, form pick on ratings
runners_data.comment: Second in a 7f maiden at Dundalk on debut, failed to show improvement on her second AW run
runners_data.spotlight: Bought for 160,000euros last May; two encouraging opening efforts when hitting the frame in 7f Dundalk maidens late last year; found only the Group 1-entered Glyfada too good at Killarney (1m, good) on return 17 days ago; the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Miss Moore Cen
runners_data.note: Struggled on debut at the Curragh and needs significant improvement from midfield finish
runners_data.spotlight: Very capable young trainer but will need to step up a lot on midfield finish at the Curragh (6f) on debut when behind Cactus.

runners_data.name: Due In June
runners_data.note: Made little impression on debut 11 days ago but wears hood for first time today
runners_data.comment: Half-sister to a winner at around 7f, stable's Flat wins typically with older horses
runners_data.spotlight: Made little impression in 7.5f maiden claimer at Roscommon on debut 11 days ago; hooded.

runners_data.name: Justiciar
runners_data.note: Highest-rated on 83 but disappointing since promising debut third, wears tongue-tie and blinkers
runners_data.spotlight: Top-rated in the field with a mark of 83; promise on Curragh debut (7f, good) last June when 1.5l third behind Composing (peak rating 110); disappointing since, including on handicap debut at the Curragh (7f) on latest; headgear needs to bring out improvement.

runners_data.name: Croi Gra
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who raced too keenly when third on debut but can control tempo here
runners_data.comment: Respectable debut at a big price in a Gowran race dominated by market leaders, can improve
runners_data.spotlight: Respectable debut when third at a big price in 1m Gowran maiden dominated by market leaders; raced far too keenly and built up big early advantage before weakening on next start at Navan (1m2f); drop in trip may help.

runners_data.name: Cactus
runners_data.note: Well-exposed and regressive with fourth place finish on return after poor back-end to last season
runners_data.spotlight: Well exposed daughter of Wootton Bassett out of a mare by Galileo; regressive tail end of last year; fourth of 24 in 6f Curragh maiden (soft) on return; hard to be confident despite the pedigree, connections and being Aidan O'Brien's sole runner on the card.

runners_data.name: Hasita
runners_data.note: Caught the eye when never-nearer third at Cork but has habit of fading in the closing stages
runners_data.comment: Needs to step up on the form of two juvenile outings at the Curragh, yard's second string
runners_data.spotlight: Contested two very strong Curragh maidens last May/June as a juvenile; returned with eyecatching never-nearer third of 15 at Cork (6f, soft); wasn't given a hard time and every chance with Ben Coen back aboard if she handles quicker ground.

runners_data.name: Wearing Stars
runners_data.note: Twice placed on all-weather but struggled in latest handicap start, wears tongue-tie today
runners_data.comment: Twice placed over 6f on AW; should come on from reappearance fourth at Cork (5f, soft)
runners_data.spotlight: Twice placed over 6f on AW late last year; fourth in 5f Cork maiden on reappearance; never in contention on 6f handicap debut at Naas last month; others are more likely for win purposes.

races.paceDynamic: Croi Gra will be the sole pace-setter from her inside draw, with her confirmed front-running style and tendency to race keenly creating a solo lead scenario. The prominent runners What About Us, Justiciar, Cactus, Hasita and Wearing Stars will settle behind her in a chasing pack, while the hold-up horses Rebel Wave and Due In June drop back further. With only one speed horse in a 14-runner field, Croi Gra can dictate terms at a sustainable gallop before the field closes late. This race shape strongly favours prominent racers who can track the leader and kick clear, as they avoid both the pressure of making the running and the traffic problems of hold-up horses in a large field.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Croi Gra Controls Tempo
scenarios.trigger: If Croi Gra settles better than her previous keen display and isn't pressured for the lead.
scenarios.body: She can dictate a moderate pace and prove hard to peg back when the field comes to challenge her in the straight. Her previous third at Gowran showed ability when not racing too keenly, and the solo lead scenario plays to her strengths.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Trackers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If the chasing pack gets into a rhythm behind Croi Gra and can unleash a sustained challenge.
scenarios.body: What About Us and Justiciar have the class edge with their previous form figures and can time their runs to perfection from tracking positions. Their superior ratings and tactical speed give them the edge over the exposed pace-setter.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Kick Succeeds
scenarios.trigger: If Croi Gra goes too fast early and the pace collapses, creating gaps for closers.
scenarios.body: Rebel Wave showed promise on debut despite needing the run and can improve significantly with that experience under her belt. The strong pedigree and yard form give her each-way claims if the race falls apart up front.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Unconsidered Newcomer Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the debutants with strong pedigrees show significantly more ability than their market prices suggest.
scenarios.body: Dandymaria brings the best breeding as sister to a Listed-placed winner, while trainer Oliver is in decent form. The lack of form gives these horses mystery value if the exposed runners underperform.

watchPoints.text: Croi Gra must settle better than her keen debut display or she will empty out in the closing stages having done too much early
What About Us carries strong form credentials but returns from a 17-day break which may leave her needing the run
Several expensive debutants including Dandymaria and Sioux The Boss could show significant improvement on their breeding
The large field of 14 runners creates traffic concerns for hold-up horses like Rebel Wave who need clear runs
Justiciar wears blinkers and tongue-tie suggesting connections are trying to spark improvement after disappointing efforts

races.name: BOYLE Sports Extra Places Every Day Handicap

runners_data.name: Imperial Dream
runners_data.note: Prominent runner whose close fourth in this race last year off higher weight gives him a strong profile here
runners_data.comment: C&D winner on quick ground in August 2024, only flashes of his best form last year
runners_data.spotlight: Close fourth over C&D at this meeting in 2024 off 74; last win at the Curragh (6f, good) in August of that year; has largely struggled for form since.

runners_data.name: Charming Whisper
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who needs the gaps to open up; headgear applied suggests connections seeking improvement
runners_data.spotlight: Won five times when trained in Britain by Philip McBride; all those wins came on ground with good in the description; slowly away and always behind at the Curragh on latest; new headgear.

runners_data.name: Shoot To Kill
runners_data.note: Prominent style suits this pace scenario perfectly; 10lb drop in ratings plus 5lb claimer makes him well-handicapped
runners_data.comment: Won this last year, effectively 13lb lower here with rider's claim,  don't discount
runners_data.spotlight: Two wins last year on good ground for different trainers, including 7.5f Roscommon handicap off 80; now 10lb lower plus talented claimer takes off another 5lb; got his favoured ground when eyecatching third of 14 at Roscommon from tough draw 18 days ago; big chance.

runners_data.name: Amemri
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who showed return to form at Dundalk; needs this race to come back to him late
runners_data.comment: Recorded tenth win under rules' on AW last month; C&D winner last year off 5lb higher
runners_data.spotlight: Back to form when recording a tenth career win at Dundalk in March; has won three times on turf and finished runner-up of 15 at Limerick (1m, yielding) on latest when just in front of Minaun View; player.

runners_data.name: Rappell
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse struggling for form this season; needs significant improvement to feature
runners_data.spotlight: Three turf wins, the latest at the Curragh in 2024; added a 6f AW win last September; needs to step up considerably on the form of this season's four outings.

runners_data.name: Faoladh
runners_data.note: Prominent runner in good form; third at Leopardstown recently shows he's competitive at this level
runners_data.comment: C&D winner last June off 2lb lower, has a bit to find with Monvoe on Limerick running
runners_data.spotlight: Enjoyed a good spell last summer, winning at Leopardstown (1m, good) off 1lb lower; fair efforts in defeat this year, including third at Leopardstown a fortnight ago; likely to be in the shake-up.

runners_data.name: Minaun View
runners_data.note: Prominent maiden who ran well behind Amemri last time; consistent placing record suggests each-way claims
runners_data.comment: 0-14, decent run at Limerick latest, nicely drawn, place shout if gets in; reserve
runners_data.spotlight: Third runner for yard; maiden after 15 starts; one of her better runs when 3l third of 15 at Limerick (1m, yielding; one place behind Amemri) on penultimate; best work late on when fifth of 14 at Roscommon (7.5f, good) on latest; place shout.

runners_data.name: Dynamic Force
runners_data.note: Prominent horse who was runner-up in this race last year; 8lb lower now but poor recent form
runners_data.comment: On a long losing sequence and lacks a recent run, very capable rider claims 7lb
runners_data.spotlight: Speedy in his early days, winning three times over 5f for Robert Cowell; runner-up when sent off favourite for this race (good) last year; 8lb lower now but on a long losing sequence and weakened at Leopardstown on return.

runners_data.name: Land Of The Giants
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse in excellent form with recent Ayr win; back on turf after good runs
runners_data.comment: Stall advantaged over trip, expected to go really well
runners_data.spotlight: Second runner for yard; in good form on turf recently, with a breakthrough win at Ayr (1m1f, good to firm) off 63 at the start of the month; fairly treated back on home soil but below his best in two starts since, including Dundalk claimer on Tuesday.

runners_data.name: Una Matata
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse making seasonal turf debut; excellent AW form but question marks over surface switch
runners_data.comment: Didn't land a blow a week ago from wide draw in handicap but respected back in a claimer
runners_data.spotlight: First turf run since September last year; excellent record on AW of late, winning four of her last 10 starts, three at this trip; one place behind Thaloria when third in 7f claimer there when last seen; tough mark back on grass.

runners_data.name: Eichan San
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who stays strongly; drop back from 5f sprint last time should suit better
runners_data.spotlight: Now 0-8 but has ability judged on his keeping-on fourth of 21 at the Curragh on penultimate (6f, soft); the drop to 5f was a bad move last time (outpaced) but can't rule out a big run over this trip.

runners_data.name: Goldsmith
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse making seasonal debut after 231 days off; mostly disappointing for current yard
runners_data.spotlight: Third reserve; five AW wins when trained in Britain; mostly below form for this yard.

runners_data.name: Bay Of Dreams
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who has been disappointing since yard switch; well behind Faoladh last time
runners_data.comment: Highly consistent in Britain last year, tailed off on stable debut when badly hampered
runners_data.spotlight: Won twice for James Ferguson last year, including on turf at Nottingham; tailed off in two starts for this yard, behind third-placed Faoladh at Leopardstown on latest.

runners_data.name: Thaloria
runners_data.note: Prominent horse whose Dundalk win doesn't translate to turf; completely tailed off last turf start
runners_data.comment: Dundalk winner, needs to step up on the form of her Leopardstown run last month
runners_data.spotlight: Stepped up markedly on maiden runs when scoring on handicap debut at Dundalk in January over 7f; not as effective on turf and was completely tailed off in 1m Curragh handicap (good) on Sunday; eased in grade but others preferred.

runners_data.name: Lohengrin
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with poor recent form; Colin Keane booking interesting but needs major improvement
runners_data.comment: Only win from 27 starts gained in a 7f maiden at Laytown, his trainer's local track
runners_data.spotlight: Won 7f Laytown maiden last September; poor winter form at Dundalk; brought down at Bellewstown on return; in rear at Navan and Roscommon; Colin Keane is 0-8 on him; looks vulnerable.

runners_data.name: Brains
runners_data.note: Natural front-runner who sets the tactical template; at 10 years old brings experience to lead this field
runners_data.comment: Won over C&D at this meeting two years ago and ran well at Leopardstown on seasonal debut
runners_data.spotlight: Second reserve; seventh in this race last year; not beaten far on last two runs; in the mix.

runners_data.name: Burford Beauty
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with fair handicap form; stalls issues could compromise her chances from the gates
runners_data.comment: Just fair form in h'caps but mark is dropping; fifth of 13 when last seen on turf
runners_data.spotlight: First reserve; just fair form in handicaps to date, including fifth over C&D; can get upset in the stalls.

races.paceDynamic: Brains is the sole confirmed front-runner in this large field and will likely set his own fractions without early pressure, creating a sustainable pace that could be too slow for the finish. Imperial Dream, Shoot To Kill, Faoladh, Minaun View, Dynamic Force and Thaloria can sit prominent behind him, but none are natural speed merchants. The large field of 17 and lack of pace pressure means the tempo will build gradually, with the real action coming late as the hold-up horses get organized from midfield and rear. This race shape strongly favours the prominent and midfield runners who can position handy and have something left to kick, while the pure hold-up horses may find themselves with too much to do from the back of this big field.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Moderate Pace Benefits Prominent
scenarios.trigger: If Brains sets sensible fractions and the prominent horses get ideal positioning behind him
scenarios.body: The race builds steadily with plenty left for the finish, suiting horses that can track the pace and quicken. Shoot To Kill and Faoladh are perfectly positioned to capitalize with their prominent styles and recent form.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Get Lucky
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely slow and the field comes back to the closers in the final furlong
scenarios.body: Land Of The Giants and Amemri get the perfect setup to unleash their finishing kicks from off the pace. The sustainable gallop allows patient tactics to pay dividends as the early leaders weaken.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Gets Away
scenarios.trigger: If Brains is allowed to dictate completely uncontested and the field gets strung out
scenarios.body: The lack of early pace pressure allows the leader to build an unassailable advantage as the field spreads out behind. Dynamic Force could benefit from tracking the uncontested leader while others struggle to get involved.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Messy Large Field Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the big field causes traffic problems and interference in the straight as horses look for racing room
scenarios.body: The race becomes a lottery with positioning crucial and several runners getting blocked or checked. Horses drawn favorably or with tactical speed to avoid trouble benefit from others' misfortune.

watchPoints.text: Brains is the key tactical factor as the only front-runner; if he breaks slowly or gets headed early the whole race shape changes
Traffic problems are highly likely in this 17-runner field when they turn for home and the hold-up horses look for racing room
Una Matata making her turf seasonal debut after excellent AW form; watch how she handles the surface switch
Several horses including Burford Beauty and Charming Whisper have stalls issues that could ruin their chances before the race begins
The prominent horses Imperial Dream, Shoot To Kill and Faoladh all have recent course form that gives them a key advantage

races.name: BOYLE Sports Home Of The Early Payout Handicap

runners_data.name: Thistle Cross
runners_data.note: Front-runner with fade tendency, 14 days since poor seasonal debut, needs to prove turf form
runners_data.comment: Couple of modest AW efforts late last year, easily overlooked now on turf debut
runners_data.spotlight: Couple of modest AW efforts late last year; completely tailed off on turf/seasonal debut; easily overlooked despite now handicapping.

runners_data.name: Andosky

runners_data.comment: Soundly beaten both starts in soft this term; has to improve for this ground down in trip

runners_data.name: Fontaine Khaled

runners_data.spotlight: Nice run in good-ground Curragh maiden last year; well held first two handicap starts but not beaten too far in much better race than this at Naas (6f) last month; wouldn't be too quick to dismiss her.

runners_data.name: Sand Art
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning after 107 days, shown little improvement for handicapping
runners_data.comment: Reserve; well beaten in three m'dens and no sign of improvement in h'cap last time
runners_data.spotlight: Well beaten in three maidens and no sign of improvement for switch to handicaps at Dundalk last time.

runners_data.name: Meriden
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who stayed on well in handicap debut at Ballinrobe, suits this longer trip
runners_data.spotlight: Never threatened in trio of maidens at 6f-1m on soft/AW; got going late when sixth of 13 on handicap debut at Ballinrobe (9.5f, good to yielding) three weeks ago; others preferred.

runners_data.name: Bullet Bourbon
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with slow-break issues, fade tendency but best form at Dundalk
runners_data.comment: Penultimate Dundalk second puts her in the mix here
runners_data.spotlight: Maiden went closest when chasing home a progressive type over 6f at Dundalk in April; slowly away over 7f at Gowran next time; another slow break over 6f at Navan on latest; others more likely.

runners_data.name: Another Nice'day
runners_data.note: Hold-up type returning after 191 days, cheekpieces applied, previously respectable here
runners_data.spotlight: Respectable fifth at this course over 5f in her first handicap in September, staying on after taking a hold in first-time cheekpieces; failed to see out this trip at Dundalk next time; gelded ahead of return.

runners_data.name: Sweet Baby Zou
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner from in-form O'Brien yard (10/60), looked in need of this trip last start
runners_data.spotlight: No sign of winning potential in three qualifying runs at 6f-1m2f on testing ground; looked in need of further when seventh of 14 at Roscommon (7.5f, good) on handicap debut but can't rule out for top yard.

runners_data.name: Dervo Annie
runners_data.note: Front-runner from small yard, 48 days since last run, never threatened in handicap debut
runners_data.comment: Soundly beaten in trio of maidens at Navan/Dundalk over 5f-7f; market will provide clues

races.paceDynamic: Thistle Cross and Dervo Annie will contest the early lead, with both confirmed front-runners likely to set an honest gallop over this 7f trip. Queen Of Newark and Fontaine Khaled should track prominently behind the leaders, while the bulk of the field including Imnotleavinyou, Sweet Baby Zou and Beau Army will settle further back. With multiple horses showing fade warnings and several proven late finishers, the contested early pace will set up perfectly for hold-up horses to mount challenges in the final 2f. This pace scenario strongly favours horses with proven finishing kicks who can close from off the pace.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Strong Early Gallop
scenarios.trigger: If Thistle Cross and Dervo Annie both go forward aggressively from the start.
scenarios.body: The honest pace will stretch the field and expose those with stamina limitations, allowing closers like Imnotleavinyou and Meriden to pick up the pieces late. Multiple pace-setters ensures no tactical advantage for any single leader.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Moderate Contested Pace
scenarios.trigger: If one of the front-runners settles more conservatively while the other takes control.
scenarios.body: Queen Of Newark and Fontaine Khaled can track the moderate pace comfortably and strike from prominent positions in the straight. The less severe gallop suits horses that need cover but don't require maximum pace collapse.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Tactical Battle Early
scenarios.trigger: If both Thistle Cross and Dervo Annie are restrained, creating a slow early tempo.
scenarios.body: The lack of early pace will bring stamina into play and favour horses that can quicken from any position, potentially suiting Queen Of Newark's recent improved form. A sprint finish develops where positioning becomes crucial over raw pace.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If either Thistle Cross or Dervo Annie gets an uncontested lead with the other settling back.
scenarios.body: The lone leader could steal a significant advantage if the pace collapses, though both have shown tendencies to fade which makes this outcome unlikely. Would require tactical errors from prominent runners.

races.paceDynamic: Dallas Star and Mont St Michel will ensure a proper gallop from the front in this 6-runner Listed contest over 2 miles. Both confirmed leaders should contest the early pace, with Dallas Star's front-running Group 3 success suggesting he'll be aggressive from the gate. The honest tempo they create will stretch out the field on good ground, making it a test of stamina and class rather than a tactical sprint. This pace scenario clearly favours the prominent racers Tennessee Stud and Carmers, who can track the leaders and have the class to strike when the pace takes its toll.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Dallas Star and Mont St Michel set honest fractions without burning each other up
scenarios.body: The sustained pace will find out the hold-up horses over this staying trip, allowing Tennessee Stud and Carmers to use their superior class ratings from tracking positions. Their Group-level experience becomes decisive in the final furlong when the leaders weaken.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Survives
scenarios.trigger: If Dallas Star gets an uncontested lead with Mont St Michel failing to go the pace
scenarios.body: The Brazilian-trained gelding can dictate terms and use his proven front-running ability to steal a march on classier rivals. His Group 3 Ballysax success shows he can win at this level when allowed to control the tempo.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Kick Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is strong enough to set up Layfayette's closing kick from the rear
scenarios.body: The veteran's ten wins include success over testing trips, and Colin Keane can time his challenge perfectly if the leaders go too fast. His recent Curragh win shows he retains his finishing kick at age nine.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Course Specialist Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Alba Chiara can reproduce her Ulster Cesarewitch winning form at this track
scenarios.body: Her 2m2f course success last September proves she handles Down Royal's unique characteristics better than rivals. The 10lb weight advantage could be decisive if the pace collapses into a sprint finish.

races.paceDynamic: Tassarolo stands out as the sole confirmed front runner and will dictate terms from the start. With Pons Aelius and Velvet And Vine as the only prominent runners, there's minimal early pressure which allows Tassarolo to control a steady gallop. The large field of hold-up horses creates a bunched pack behind the leaders, setting up a cavalry charge finish over the final 3-4 furlongs. This sustainable pace scenario strongly favours hold-up horses who can produce their best turn of foot late, while the lack of pace pressure makes life difficult for prominent runners trying to track the leader.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sustained Kick Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Tassarolo sets an uncontested lead and the pace stays modest throughout
scenarios.body: The patient hold-up horses get the perfect setup with plenty left in the tank for a strong finish. Class horses like Mephisto and Jurality can unleash their best over the final furlong when fresher rivals tire.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Survives
scenarios.trigger: If Tassarolo gets away with a very slow pace and kicks clear turning for home
scenarios.body: With minimal early exertion, Tassarolo has enough left to resist the late challengers who find the gap closing too slowly. The prominent runners struggle in no-man's land as the kick comes too late.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Mid-Race Pressure Changes
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent runners apply unexpected pressure to Tassarolo from halfway
scenarios.body: The increased tempo stretches the field and favours horses with tactical speed who can position closer. Those held up too far back find the gap unbridgeable when the pace lifts.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Complete Collapse Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is glacially slow and everyone finishes strongly
scenarios.body: The race becomes a pure sprint finish where the best turn of foot wins regardless of position. Fresh horses with natural speed dominate while stamina becomes irrelevant over the shortened sprint distance.

races.paceDynamic: Misty Cove is the only confirmed front runner and will likely get an uncontested lead with Harmani, Oust and Sutton Hoo tracking prominently but not pressuring early. The pace should be steady rather than strong with the majority of the field (Eniac, Pierre Grosse, Another Day Done, Chapel Lane, Chestnut Palace, Vantage Code, Lord Aus, Grey Intentions) settling in behind looking for late runs. This creates a race where the early leaders can establish position without pressure, then dictate terms in the straight. The tactical verdict clearly favours prominent runners who can track the pace and kick, as hold-up horses will face traffic problems with nine runners needing room late.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Trackers Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the pace stays steady and Misty Cove maintains control without excessive pressure.
scenarios.body: Harmani and Pierre Grosse can track the leader and have first run in the straight while the hold-up brigade get shuffled back. Their superior tactical position allows them to strike before the backmarkers can organize their challenges.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Sustainability
scenarios.trigger: If Misty Cove gets completely uncontested fractions and kicks clear turning in.
scenarios.body: The lack of early pace pressure allows the leader to save energy for a sustained finish that the prominent trackers cannot match. Oust could emerge as the main danger having shown he handles positive tactics.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Charge Success
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is genuinely crawling and the race becomes a sprint from the two pole.
scenarios.body: The compressed field allows talented hold-up horses like Eniac and Another Day Done to weave through and time their runs perfectly. Chapel Lane's strong finishing kick becomes a major weapon in this scenario.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Longshot Breakthrough
scenarios.trigger: If traffic problems and pace collapse create chaos in the straight with fallers and interference.
scenarios.body: An outsider like Sutton Hoo or Rapide Vega gets a dream run through gaps while the fancied runners are stopped in their tracks. The race becomes a lottery where position and luck matter more than ability.

runners_data.spotlight: All four runs have been over 7f/1m, showing mild promise in Leopardstown maiden but no improvement dropped to claiming company latest; marked step up in trip here.

runners_data.name: Divelment
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who disappointed when overdoing forcing tactics last time, wears cheekpieces
runners_data.comment: Rated 69, best treated by race conditions, new headgear combo, the one to beat if fit
runners_data.spotlight: Placed twice in maidens at Roscommon last year and again twice over this trip on the AW early this year; overdid the forcing tactics when disappointing in Ballinrobe claimer on latest, claimed afterwards for 5,000euros; definite chance on his best form.

runners_data.name: Kingcharles
runners_data.note: Fading finisher with modest form who likely needs handicap company
runners_data.comment: Always behind on Navan debut last month, easily passed over
runners_data.spotlight: Couple of modest runs of late, likely to need more time and handicaps.

runners_data.name: Tavarua
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse whose two runs came on soft ground, step up in trip should suit
runners_data.spotlight: Both runs last month came in soft-ground Gowran maidens over a mile; this longer trip should suit but good bit of improvement required.

runners_data.name: Amrum
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who has looked limited in three runs, likely needs handicap company
runners_data.comment: Half-brother to Irish 2,000 Guineas winner Siskin, no sign of winning potential so far
runners_data.spotlight: Half-brother to Irish 2,000 Guineas winner Siskin; has looked limited in three maiden runs this spring and looks a more likely one for handicaps although this grade of maiden offers possibilities.

runners_data.name: Avec Grand Plaisir
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with just okay form, another handicap candidate
runners_data.comment: Soundly beaten in maidens at the Curragh and Leopardstown five months apart
runners_data.spotlight: Just okay runs this term in maidens at Leopardstown and Roscommon; another for whom handicaps beckon.

runners_data.name: Second Line
runners_data.note: Fading finisher who failed to stay 1m2f previously, needs significant improvement
runners_data.comment: Excuse for a poor run at two, hard to make a case for him based on a Dundalk outing
runners_data.spotlight: Hasn't troubled the judge in three runs, second occasion not looking to stay 1m2f; needs to improve plenty.

runners_data.name: Espritroyale
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who improved for stable switch but took backward step latest
runners_data.comment: Better effort on stable debut latest, worth a market check in first handicap
runners_data.spotlight: No show in two maidens for Sheila Lavery last year; improved effort in 6f Curragh maiden on debut for this yard in March but took a backward step in Roscommon handicap since; big step up in trip here (half-sister to 1m4f winner).

races.paceDynamic: Divelment is the only confirmed front-runner and will dictate proceedings, likely to get an uncontested lead through reasonable fractions at this staying trip. The prominent runners Nermal, Maxminelli, and Moon Vega will track but won't apply serious early pressure, while the large contingent of hold-up horses including Teologia, Gatlinburg, and Cosmic Funk will need the pace to develop. With minimal early pace pressure and a single leader, this sets up perfectly for the hold-up horses who can position patiently and finish strongly, making this a race that clearly favours patient, closing types over those needing to race prominently.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-up horses dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Divelment sets steady fractions without pressure from the prominent runners
scenarios.body: The patient closers get the perfect setup to deliver late runs from off the pace. Teologia and Gatlinburg benefit most from their recent form improvements and this tactical scenario.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent runners capitalise
scenarios.trigger: If Nermal or Maxminelli apply more pressure to Divelment than expected
scenarios.body: The increased pace stretches the field and suits those who can travel strongly in behind the leaders before quickening. Both Nermal and Maxminelli have shown recent improvement and can exploit this scenario.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Divelment wires field
scenarios.trigger: If the front-runner gets very soft fractions and kicks clear approaching the straight
scenarios.body: His previous placings show he can be effective when not overdoing the pace-forcing tactics. The lack of early pressure allows him to conserve energy for a sustained finish.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider breakthrough
scenarios.trigger: If the principals fail to fire and a lightly-raced improver emerges
scenarios.body: Moon Vega or Cosmic Funk could benefit from the step up in trip and take advantage if the market leaders underperform. The maiden nature means unexposed types can find significant improvement.

watchPoints.text: Divelment could get uncontested fractions and prove hard to peg back if he doesn't overdo the forcing tactics
Maxminelli's tongue-tie had immediate effect last time and prominent position could prove decisive
Teologia's late-running style perfectly suits the likely scenario with minimal early pace
Several horses including Gatlinburg and Second Line have shown fading tendencies in recent runs
Moon Vega and Cosmic Funk face significant distance tests having not raced beyond 1m previously
